headline: Multimodal learning advances biomedical interaction and function prediction
label: Multimodal Representation Learning For Biomedicine
summary: Recent August 2026 publications combine graph networks, LLM-derived text and self-supervised pretraining for drug, protein and gene prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is multimodal representation learning that integrates heterogeneous biological inputs through graph neural architectures and attention-based fusion. Several items combine molecular structure, sequence, knowledge graph and interaction-network features for drug-target, drug-drug and biomedical interaction prediction (MVR-DTI, OMNI, FGSGT-DDI). GatedGeoGO fuses sequence, 3D structure, PPI and GO semantics via gated fusion and reports gains over baselines on low-frequency GO terms. What is comparatively new is the use of language-model outputs as an input modality: TextDTI aligns LLM-generated protein function text with SMILES and graph encodings, and FGSGT-DDI uses LLM-derived functional group semantic embeddings. Protein language model embeddings (ProtT5) underpin the peptide classifier TPpred-PepPA. SDMGAE is a label-free dual-masked graph autoencoder for cancer driver gene identification on PPI networks, and a review covers self-supervised molecular property prediction.
